- Overestimate early in the forecast horizon when sentiment is positive (especially >0.5) — adjust downward by 1–3% for the first 5–7 days.
- Underestimate when sentiment is negative (especially <0.0) — add 2–5% to forecast for the first 3–5 days.
- Avoid sharp downward spikes in forecast after recent price spikes — model tends to overcorrect; apply a “lagged momentum” filter: if last 3 days show upward momentum, cap forecast decline at 10% below prior peak.
- Mean-reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 5-day average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- Overshoot after sentiment spikes: if sentiment >0.75 and price rises >5%, reduce forecast by 2–4% for next 3–5 days to avoid overbought overcorrection.
- Horizon-specific: for 30-day forecasts, last 5–7 days of forecast should align with recent sentiment trend — if sentiment is trending up, forecast should not dip below 10% below prior 5-day average.
